text:
julia-cs: hey team, customer (acme-app) reporting repeated 503s and timeouts starting ~09:02 UTC, says spikes last 30–60s and then recover. they sent an example request id: r-8f3b. stacktrace in their logs shows upstream_worker_exit, container restarted. canops pls triage :exclamation:

mike-eng: looking. I see spike in hosted gateway p50->p95 at 09:02. Correlating with runner restarts in cluster-7. Pulling node logs now.

sre-oncall: I see deploy-bot note for a canary model swap at 08:59: `deploy-bot: canary model swap v2-quant -> v3-large started by kevin-ml` — could be related.

kevin-ml: that canary was for a quantized variant, landed 08:59 in a small pool. we didn't expect memory increase. Did customer include prompt size?

julia-cs: customer says long prompt ~80k tokens (embedding + system) but they were previously OK with v2-quant.

mike-eng: grabbing runner logs from host-a12:
```
[2021-10-01T09:02:15Z] runtime: aborting: double free or heap smash detected
[2021-10-01T09:02:16Z] infer-worker(2345): segfault (signal 11) at 0x000000
[2021-10-01T09:02:16Z] kernel: Out of memory: Kill process 2345 (infer-worker) score 987 or sacrifice child
[2021-10-01T09:02:17Z] containerd: restarting container infer-worker
```

sre-oncall: logs show both heap corruption 'double free' and GPU memory ballooning. nvml reports OOM on device 0 preceding the segfault.

kevin-ml: interesting — quant swap should reduce memory. maybe a regression in allocator path under long-seq workload. repro plan: run their prompt against v3-large and v2-quant locally in staging with same batch config.

mike-eng: quick mitigation: rolling back canary to v2-quant and draining cluster-7 workers from hosted-gateway routing. I've pushed a traffic rule to divert 100% away from pool-7.

deploy-bot: rollback enacted by mike-eng at 2021-10-01T09:05:40Z: model pool-7 -> v2-quant (safe).

julia-cs: customer confirmed their requests recovered around 09:06. they want RCA and repro steps.

kevin-ml: next steps for repro:
1) run their exact prompt (they provided anonymized) with seq_len=80k and batch_size=1 under debug build with ASAN off but heap-checking on.
2) run with `--force-quant=false` and `--force-quant=true` to compare allocator behavior.
3) enable nvml logging and capture dmesg.

mike-eng: adding checklist for postmortem notes:
- capture core dump from affected worker (we have coredump at /var/crash/infer-worker-2345.core)
- copy nvml logs and `nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY` output from before restart
- compare memory footprint between v2-quant and v3-large on same prompt
- check kernel OOM timestamps vs runtime segfault timestamp to determine cause vs effect

sre-oncall: temporary operational guard: add a limiter on sequence length per request for hosted gateway to 60k until we fix allocator path. I'll open a small policy PR.

julia-cs: customer asked about billing for failed requests — they were charged for some failed tokens. CS will escalate billing if there's mismatch after logs.

kevin-ml: I'll try to reproduce now in staging and post logs here. if I can reproduce, will bisect change in quant allocator.

mike-eng: thanks. tagging oncall to watch for any re-occurrence: @sre-oncall please monitor cluster-7 for 24h and alert if >3 restarts in 1h.

sre-oncall: ack. setting alert and will post an update in this thread.

julia-cs: summarizing for ticket: customer experienced gateway 503s due to upstream worker crash during a canary model swap under a very long prompt, temporary rollback applied, customer recovered, CS follow-up on billing. will add links to logs and core dump in the ticket. :white_check_mark:
